summary.text: 山 is a pictograph of mountain peaks standing together. Its common meaning is “mountain”; “hill” and “peak” are also recorded glosses.

formation.text: The whole graph is a pictograph depicting mountain peaks, rather than a combination of separate semantic or phonetic parts. Paleographic records list oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal and Shuowen forms.

components.text: The whole graph 山 depicts mountain peaks standing together; it is an indivisible pictorial form, not a set of smaller components.

history.text: The paleographic record lists 山 in several script stages but does not establish a continuous sequence of graphic changes. The selected small-seal-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient specimen; its peaks and curved base illustrate the pictograph.

A Han-period dictionary account says that 山 disperses qi, gives rise to the myriad things, and is high with rocks, then labels the graph pictographic. This is a historical interpretation, not confirmation of the graph’s original meaning.

uncertainties.text: The available account does not establish the date or lexical value of the earliest specimen, precise dates for the listed forms, or a continuous graphic development.

senses.text: The ordinary landscape-noun sense is supported, but its earliest attestation and deeper chronology remain unresolved.
“Hill” is also recorded as a gloss. The evidence does not establish when this use arose relative to “mountain.”
“Peak” is also recorded as a gloss; no separate historical development from the landscape noun is established.

limitations.text: A Shijing phrase uses 山 in a landscape context, but the available record does not establish the poem’s composition date or earliest physical witness. No earlier lexical sense or semantic transition is established.

overview.text: 山 pictures mountain peaks standing together and commonly means “mountain”; “hill” and “peak” are also recorded glosses.

components.text: The whole character pictures mountain peaks standing together.
